summary: This photocycloaddition reaction utilizes triplet sensitization with 2,2'-dimethoxythioxanthone (2,2'-MeOTX) as the photocatalyst at 1 mol% loading under 455 nm COB LED irradiation. The flow process operates in acetonitrile at 200°C with a 5-minute residence time and 6.0 mL/min flow rate using a FlowSyn steel coil reactor (30 mL volume) equipped with a 34 bar back-pressure regulator. Flow chemistry enabled daisy-chaining of the initial photochemical step with high-temperature thermal cascade reactions, dramatically improving yield from 16% in batch (2 hours) to 88% in flow with a 24-fold intensification factor. The high-temperature operation required for the thermal cascade was much safer to implement in the continuous flow reactor compared to batch processing.

summary: This photoredox cross-coupling reaction utilizes single electron transfer (SET) mechanism with Ir[dF(CF3)ppy]2(dtbbpy)PF6 photocatalyst (2 mol%) and tBu-TMG base in DMF solvent under 440 nm blue LED irradiation. The optimized flow process operates at 50°C with a 12-minute residence time at 0.83 mL/min flow rate in a segmented flow reactor using FEP tubing with 10 mL reactor volume. Flow conditions achieved 88% yield compared to 81% yield under batch conditions at 30°C, representing an 8.6% improvement in yield. The primary advantage of flow was enabling higher operating temperature (50°C vs 30°C) with superior heat transfer control, while providing predictable scale-up capability to hundreds of mg/h production rates with significantly shorter reaction times.

summary: This photochemical C-H functionalization reaction uses a hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) mechanism followed by electrochemical oxidation, employing FeCl3 (5 mol%) as the photocatalyst under 390 nm LED irradiation in acetonitrile solvent. The flow process operates in an f-EPC reactor with a 1.2 mL volume using stainless steel and PTFE frames, achieving 88% yield with a 15-minute residence time at 0.08 mL/min flow rate. Flow chemistry provided a dramatic 16-fold reduction in reaction time compared to the 4-hour batch process while improving yield from 80% to 88%. The flow advantage stems from enhanced heat and mass transfer in the continuous operation, along with better light penetration efficiency in the smaller reactor volume. The shorter residence time and higher yield demonstrate the superior performance of flow photochemistry for this C-H activation transformation.
